title: Service: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer and DNS discovery

videos.script: Pods come and go, and each new one has a new address. Nothing that calls the shop can keep a list of them. {{come}} A Service is the fixed point. It has one address that never changes, and one name in the cluster's DNS. Behind it, the cluster keeps a list of whichever pods carry the right label, right now. {{fixed}} You will read that list, find the Service by name from inside a pod, and empty the list, to see what a caller gets then. {{empty}} Then you will reach the shop from outside, two ways. A port on every node. And a load balancer, with an address of its own, the way a cloud provides one. {{outside}} The three types are not alternatives. Each one is built on the one before. {{built}}
